                         OPPOSITION OF DEFENDANT
          THE NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN
     TO PLAINTIFF’S MOTION TO VACATE HEARING SET FOR SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

        Defendant the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children [“NCMEC”], by and

through undersigned counsel and pursuant to the Rules and Orders of this Honorable Court,

hereby respectfully opposes Plaintiff’s “Motion to Vacate the September 30, 2026 Hearing and to

Decide the Motion to Dismiss on the Papers.” [Doc. 42] The Motion filed by the Pro Se

Plaintiff fails to state any good cause for the relief requested.

        Plaintiff appears to base his motion on two grounds, neither of which merit the relief

requested. First, Plaintiff asserts that he “does not require oral argument…” Doc. 42 at ¶ 2.

Second, Plaintiff asserts that because he is pro se, and resides in Florida, “attendance at the

hearing would require interstate travel and its attendant expense to argue a motion…” Id. at ¶ 3.

Taking these arguments in order, the hearing was not set for Plaintiff’s benefit or to ensure he

had a full opportunity to be heard. However, given Plaintiff’s pro se status, NCMEC believes

that a hearing would be a useful opportunity for the parties to be heard.

Second, Plaintiff has intentionally availed himself of this Court, and cannot credibly

complain that litigating a matter in this Court is inconvenient or carries undue expense. This

matter is the second lawsuit filed by Plaintiff against NCMEC and its employee, co-defendant

Katie Hall, Esq., and these lawsuits have carried significant inconvenience and expense to

NCMEC, and have served as an unnecessary distraction of resources from NCMEC’s core

missions.1 As a matter of common sense, when one files suit in a given District Court, one must

expect that he or she will be required to travel to the Court for court appearances. Neither of the

grounds set forth by Plaintiff constitute good cause; they simply constitute what Plaintiff feels

would be more convenient.

        In light of the foregoing, Defendant NCMEC respectfully requests that this Honorable

Court deny Plaintiff’s Motion, and that the hearing set for September 30, 2026 remain as

scheduled.




1
 Mr. Ballentine filed a complaint in Ballentine v. NCMEC, et al, Case No. 1:26-cv-01341-MSN-WBP on
May 19, 2026. On June 16, 2026, NCMEC filed a motion to dismiss. Plaintiff filed a motion for leave to
amend his complaint, which was opposed. In lieu of awaiting the Court’s ruling on either the motion to
dismiss or Plaintiff’s motion to amend, Plaintiff voluntarily dismissed that claim on July 29, 2026. The
following day, Plaintiff filed the above-captioned matter, then filed an amended complaint on August 6,
2026, and since that time has filed: a motion for partial summary judgment [Doc. 6], a motion for leave to
conduct early discovery [Doc. 15], a motion to continue the hearing on NCMEC’s motion to dismiss
[Doc. 29], a motion for leave to file a supplemental pleading [Doc. 26], a motion to appear remotely at the
hearing set for September 25 (as to Plaintiff’s own motions) [Doc. 41], the motion at issue [Doc. 42], and
has advised defense counsel of Plaintiff’s intention to file a motion for leave to file a second amended
complaint.
